LKT, an abbreviation for Lægeforeningens Kvalitetsudvalg (the Danish Medical Association's Quality Committee), is a professional advisory body involved in the clinical quality development of the Danish healthcare system. Within the context of the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen), LKT plays a role in guiding and supporting the registration and evaluation of clinical quality indicators.

The committee's involvement is noted as a positive factor in the assessment of these indicators. In the 2023 annual report, LKT's backing was specifically highlighted in relation to the registration of [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which focuses on early nutrition after surgery [^src1]. The committee's support was described as beneficial for the registration process [^src1].

By the 2024 report, which evaluated [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] (nutrition), LKT's continued support for the registration process was again acknowledged as beneficial [^src2]. However, the 2024 assessment also noted that despite this backing, there remains room for improvement in the registration practices [^src2]. This reflects the broader, ongoing narrative within the Danish healthcare system regarding the practical implementation of quality measurements, data quality, and the interplay between clinical evidence, administrative requirements, and local execution.
